To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the preoperative computed-tomography characteristics of long diameter of mass ≥4.2  cm and short diameter of lymph node ≥7 mm are predictive for the overall survival of patients with maxil-lary cancer.

the preoperative computedtomographic characteristics of tumor size and lymph node size are predictive of the overall survival time of patients with maxil-lary cancer, which could be used in practice to inform about possible prognosis and to be beneficial to clinical deci-sion making.
preoperative CT features of tumor size, cervical lymph node size and soft tissue infiltration are predictive of overall survival time of patients with maxilla cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preoperative CT characteristics that can be used in clinical decision making to predict prognosis in patients with MC.
the prognostic value and clinical significance of preoperative CT characteristics in MC patients.
the value of CT characteristics in predicting the prognosis for MC patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CT characteristics of long diameter of mass and short diameter of largest lymph node are the most efficient predictors of OS for patients with MC.
preoperative CT characteristics of long diameter of mass ≥4.2 cm, short diameter of the lymph node ≥7 mm, and adjacent structure infiltration were independent predictors for OS of MC patients.
the long diameter of the mass and the short diameter of the lymph nodes are predictive of survival time in MC patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the preoperative CT characteristics are predictive of OS for MC patients, and that the long diameter of mass ≥4.2  cm and short diameter of largest lymph node ≥7 mm are the independent predictors for OS in MC patients.
the preoperative CT characteristics of mass size, lymph node metastasis and infiltration of adjacent structures are predictive of the prognosis of MC patients.
the preoperative CT characteristics are valuable in the prediction of OS in MC patients, especially in non-epithelioid MC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CT is a powerful tool in predicting the prognosis of maxillary cancer.
the long diameter of the mass and short diameter of largest cervical lymph node could be used as a prognostic indicator for MC patients.
CT characteristics of MC patients are predictive of OS.
